display.title: My Chanukah Miracle: Recovering from COVID with Bitachon
display.summary_short: For Chanukah, the time to publicize miracles, the storyteller tells how he survived a critical case of COVID and what it taught him about bitachon and hashgachah pratis.
display.summary_long: In the spirit of Chanukah, when we spread the news of miracles, the storyteller shares his own. In the week of Purim he fell ill, was rushed to the hospital with COVID, and spent about four weeks sedated, at one point so critically ill that his family was being prepared for the worst, until Hashem turned things around. He thanks everyone who davened for him and tells of a child who said, 'davening works.' He explains the Rebbe's teaching that more years of life mean more missions, the Frierdiker Rebbe's discourse on hashgachah pratis that carried him through prison, and the Rebbe's letters on bitachon and effort. A spinning dreidel teaches that the miracles are there even when we cannot see them. He describes learning to sit, stand and walk again by picturing the Rebbe telling him to stand up, and urges listeners to keep going forward. He sings 'I Believe in Hashem' and ends with the reminder that the Geulah is perfectly planned too.
display.lesson: Hashem alone runs the world and every step is perfectly planned; our effort is needed, but the results come only from Hashem. Look for the miracles even while life is spinning.
